sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The SEC argues brokers are the critical link between markets and investors. It claims churning violates federal law. The broker argues other laws cover this conduct. Courts of appeal unanimously view churning as a violation. The dispute centers on federal liability for excessive trading.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Investors rely on brokers to act in their best interest. Excessive trading harms individual investors. Clear federal rules protect market integrity. Broker accountability ensures fair market participation. This case defines broker duties to investors.
